questions.q: Why does the lesson say contested, one-off decisions need something beyond the RACI matrix?
options: RACI is built for recurring activities, while contested decisions need sharper, pre-agreed clarity on who has final say
RACI only applies to IT departments, not governance
RACI already fully solves one-off contested decisions with no gaps
Decision rights frameworks replace the need for a RACI matrix entirely
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes RACI's fit for recurring activities from decision-rights frameworks' fit for one-off, contested decisions.

questions.q: What does the 'D' stand for in both DACI and RAPID, in spirit, according to the lesson?
options: Exactly one person or role with final decision authority
A department responsible for documentation only
A deadline with no actual decision-maker
A vote open to every stakeholder equally
questions.explain: Both DACI's Approver and RAPID's Decide isolate a single final decision-maker, named before the disagreement happens.

questions.q: In the DACI framework, what role does a Contributor play?
options: Gives input without veto power
Makes the final, binding decision
Is told the outcome only after the fact
Runs the overall decision process
questions.explain: DACI's Contributors provide input but don't hold decision authority — that belongs to the Approver.

questions.q: Which organization is credited with popularizing the RAPID decision-rights framework, per the lesson?
options: Bain & Company
Atlassian
DAMA International
A framework invented specifically for this course
questions.explain: The lesson attributes RAPID to Bain & Company, distinct from Atlassian's DACI — both are real, named frameworks, not invented ones.

questions.q: Why does the lesson argue that naming decision rights in advance reduces conflict rather than causing it?
options: Leaving "who decides" vague until the moment arrives often turns the fight personal, over who gets to decide, on top of the original question
Naming decision rights in advance is illegal unless done by a vote
Vague decision rights always resolve disputes faster
Decision rights are only relevant after a decision has already been made
questions.explain: Pre-agreeing who decides keeps attention on the actual disagreement instead of a fight over authority.
